title: Inequality-constrained lower level: primitive information and Goldstein stationarity
summary: Let $h(x,y)=Ax-By-b$, $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y:\,h(x,y)\le0}g(x,y)$, and $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$. Seek the following approximate stationarity criterion for $\min_{x\in \mathbb{R}^{d_x}}\Phi(x)$.

task.detail: min_x Phi(x) with lower feasible set {y:h(x,y)<=0}.
description_paragraphs: Let $h(x,y)=Ax-By-b$, $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y:\,h(x,y)\le0}g(x,y)$, and $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$. Seek the following approximate stationarity criterion for $\min_{x\in \mathbb{R}^{d_x}}\Phi(x)$.

model.objects: Phi(x)=f(x,y*(x)); y* uniquely minimizes g(x,y) over the declared lower feasible set.
model.regularity: f is jointly C_f-smooth and L_f-Lipschitz; g is jointly C_g-smooth and mu_y-strongly convex in y.
model.constraints: Public A in R^{d_h x d_x}, B in R^{d_h x d_y}, b in R^{d_h}; h(x,y)=Ax-By-b. B has full row rank, with public lower singular-value bound beta_B>0 and public ||A||,||B|| bounds.
model.initialization: Public x0,y0; Phi(x0)-inf Phi<=Delta, and a public lower-solution initial-distance bound R_y for cost constants/logarithms.
model.geometry: Euclidean norms; constraint matrices/data are known, not hidden oracle outputs.
model.solution_regular: The solution map y*(.) is L_y-Lipschitz; Phi is finite and globally Lipschitz. Active-set changes may make Phi nonsmooth.
description_paragraphs: The function $f$ has $C_f$-Lipschitz joint gradient and is $L_f$-Lipschitz in value. The function $g$ has $C_g$-Lipschitz joint gradient and is $\mu_y$-strongly convex in $y$. All norms are Euclidean or their induced operator norms.

Inputs $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d_h\times d_x}$, $B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_h\times d_y}$, and $b\in\mathbb{R}^{d_h}$ are public. The matrix $B$ has full row rank and smallest singular value at least the public $\beta_B>0$. The initial point has upper-level gap at most $\Delta$ and lower-level initial distance at most $R_y$.
$x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$. The solution map $y^*(\cdot)$ is $L_y$-Lipschitz. The reduced objective is finite and globally Lipschitz, but changes in the active constraints may make it nondifferentiable.
model.outer_geometry: The reduced objective may be nonconvex. Its differentiability or local Lipschitz regularity is specified by the model and accuracy measure.

operations: Choose h=f or g and (x,y); receive (h(x,y),grad h(x,y)) exactly.
oracle.auxiliary: Public A,B,b permit projections/linear constraint arithmetic; no exact multiplier, active-set, lower-solve or hypergradient oracle.
description_paragraphs: Choose function $f$ or $g$ and obtain its exact value and full gradient jointly at an admissible $(x,y)$. Queries may use the full Euclidean space.
Public linear-constraint operations and corresponding projections are free. Inner solutions, active sets, and hypergradients are not supplied implicitly.
Return an outer point $\widehat{x}\in \mathbb{R}^{d_x}$, which may be unqueried. No inner point or certificate is required.

The error is $\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_{r_G}\Phi(\widehat{x}))$, where $\partial_{r_G}\Phi(x)=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{\|z-x\|\le r_G}\partial_C\Phi(z)$; $\partial_C$ denotes the Clarke subdifferential and $r_G>0$ is the public neighborhood radius.

resource.projection: Q=N_FO_f+N_FO_g; a value-and-gradient bundle counts one selected-function call. Known-constraint arithmetic is uncharged.
description_paragraphs: Retain the two levels' primitive call counts. A joint value-and-gradient response selects one function and costs one unit; the total primitive cost is $N=N_{\mathrm{FO},f}+N_{\mathrm{FO},g}$. Every call used in an approximate inner solve is included in the fixed budget.

Arbitrary randomized adaptive algorithms are allowed, with measurable queries, stopping, and postprocessing. Outputs may be unqueried, randomly selected historical points, or admissible averages. No span or zero-respecting restriction applies. Queries are sequential; each response in a batch is charged. Internal arithmetic, linear algebra, and storage are free, with no separate work, memory, or communication budget.
For every instance, $\mathbb{E}\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_{r_G}\Phi(\widehat{x}))\le\varepsilon$. Expectation is over algorithmic randomness.

conditions: The algorithm selects the internal tolerance $\alpha$ so that $L_0^2$ dominates the bracket. This gives $\widetilde O(\sqrt{\kappa_g}d_x\Delta L_0^2/(r_G\varepsilon^3))$ for nondegenerate budgets.
applicability.dimension_conditions: The upper bound holds for every finite-dimensional instance in the declared model. Any dimension or fixed-budget dependence not displayed explicitly follows the accompanying evidence qualification.

bounds.hidden_constants: Unshown regularity, initialization, and noise budgets are fixed. Their joint parameter dependence is not certified as closed.
bounds.derivation: Use the conservative reduced-objective Lipschitz bound $L_0=L_f\sqrt{1+L_y^2}$ in the general Lipschitz analysis of Theorem C.1. Retaining the direct variation of $f$ in $x$ covers $L_y=0$.
